claim: Cavin3 is inactivated in most cancers.
source: Caveolae-associated protein 3 (cavin3) is inactivated in most cancers.
evidence: This statement is presented in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript to published literature.

claim: BRCA1 and BRCA1 A-complex components are downregulated on cavin3 deletion.
source: These studies revealed a prominent role for cavin3 in DNA repair, with BRCA1 and BRCA1 A-complex components being downregulated on cavin3 deletion.
evidence: This claim is supported by the label-free quantitative proteomics data presented in Figure 1 and western blot validation.

claim: Cavin3 directly interacts with BRCA1.
source: Cellular and cell-free expression assays revealed a direct interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3 that occurs when cavin3 is released from caveolae that are disassembled in response to UV and mechanical stress.
evidence: This is supported by single-molecule coincidence detection experiments, proximity ligation assays, and cell-free expression assays shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Cavin3 is released from caveolae in response to UV and mechanical stress.
source: Cellular and cell-free expression assays revealed a direct interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3 that occurs when cavin3 is released from caveolae that are disassembled in response to UV and mechanical stress.
evidence: This is demonstrated by PLA experiments showing increased cavin3-BRCA1 interaction and decreased cavin3-cavin1 interaction after stress treatments in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Cavin3 sensitizes various cancer cells to UV-induced apoptosis.
source: Overexpression and RNAi-depletion revealed that cavin3 sensitized various cancer cells to UV-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is supported by LDH release assays, annexin V staining, and 7-AAD staining experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Cavin3-deficient cells are sensitive to PARP inhibition.
source: Supporting a role in DNA repair, cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, where concomitant depletion of 53BP1 restored BRCA1-dependent sensitivity to PARP inhibition.
evidence: This is demonstrated by clonogenic survival assays, cell viability studies, and comet assays shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Concomitant depletion of 53BP1 in cavin3-deficient cells restores BRCA1-dependent sensitivity to PARP inhibition.
source: Supporting a role in DNA repair, cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, where concomitant depletion of 53BP1 restored BRCA1-dependent sensitivity to PARP inhibition.
evidence: This is shown in clonogenic survival and cell viability assays in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cavin3 functions together with BRCA1 in multiple cancer-related pathways.
source: We conclude that cavin3 functions together with BRCA1 in multiple cancer-related pathways.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined evidence from proteomics, interaction studies, apoptosis assays, and DNA repair experiments presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Loss of cavin3 function may provide tumor cell survival by attenuating apoptotic sensitivity and hindering DNA repair under chronic stress conditions.
source: The loss of cavin3 function may provide tumor cell survival by attenuating apoptotic sensitivity and hindering DNA repair under chronic stress conditions.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings showing reduced apoptosis and impaired DNA repair in cavin3-deficient cells.

claim: A total of 4206 proteins were robustly quantified in the label-free quantitative proteomics analysis.
source: A total of 4206 proteins were robustly quantified with >2 unique peptides and an FDR < 1.0% in at least two out of three replicates (Figure 1A, details in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mass spectrometry analysis presented in Figure 1A.

claim: Many proteins involved in DNA repair were altered in cavin3 KO cells.
source: Initial inspection of differentially expressed protein by Gene Ontology analysis revealed that many proteins involved in DNA repair were altered in cavin3 KO cells (Figure 1B, C and Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is shown in the volcano plots in Figure 1B and 1C with Gene Ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: 53BP1 protein levels were increased in cavin3 KO cells.
source: In contrast, 53BP1 protein levels were increased in cavin3 KO cells (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in the proteomics data and western blot analysis in Figure 1D.

claim: MCF7 cells lack endogenous CAV1, cavins, and caveolae.
source: These cells lack endogenous CAV1, cavins, and caveolae (Gambin et al., 2014; McMahon et al., 2019), and so expressed cavin proteins are predominantly cytosolic.
evidence: This is stated based on previous publications by the authors (Gambin et al., 2014; McMahon et al., 2019).

claim: 60% of BRCA1-GFP associated with cavin3-mCherry in MCF7 cells.
source: Quantitatively, 60% of BRCA1-GFP associated with cavin3-mCherry (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is quantified from single-molecule coincidence detection experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Overexpressed BRCA1 primarily exists in a dimeric state when expressed in MCF7 cells.
source: We concluded that overexpressed BRCA1 primarily exists in a dimeric state when expressed in MCF7 cells and that a dimer of overexpressed BRCA1 interacts with a monomer of exogenous cavin3 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is inferred from the brightness distribution analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: A dimer of overexpressed BRCA1 interacts with a monomer of exogenous cavin3.
source: We concluded that overexpressed BRCA1 primarily exists in a dimeric state when expressed in MCF7 cells and that a dimer of overexpressed BRCA1 interacts with a monomer of exogenous cavin3 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is inferred from the brightness distribution analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: A construct bearing the first 300 amino acids of BRCA1 (1-300, tr-BRCA1) was associated with cavin3 in cell-free expression assays.
source: Indeed, a construct bearing the first 300 amino acids of BRCA1 (1–300, tr-BRCA1), which contains the nuclear export signal (NES) and BARD1 binding sites (Figure 2G), was associated with cavin3 (Figure 2J), but not with the other cavin proteins (Figure 2H, I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-molecule coincidence detection in Leishmania cell-free lysates shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The first 300 amino acids of BRCA1 contain the nuclear export signal (NES) and BARD1 binding sites.
source: Indeed, a construct bearing the first 300 amino acids of BRCA1 (1–300, tr-BRCA1), which contains the nuclear export signal (NES) and BARD1 binding sites (Figure 2G), was associated with cavin3 (Figure 2J), but not with the other cavin proteins (Figure 2H, I).
evidence: This is shown in the schematic diagram in Figure 2G and is based on established knowledge of BRCA1 structure.

claim: Cavin3 binds to the N-terminus of BRCA1.
source: These data suggest that cavin3 directly binds to the N-terminus of BRCA1.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell-free expression experiments showing interaction with the 1-300 amino acid construct of BRCA1.

claim: Expression of cavin3-GFP increased cytosolic staining for endogenous BRCA1 in MCF7 cells.
source: In contrast, the expression of cavin3-GFP increased cytosolic staining for endogenous BRCA1 (Figure 4A), and this was confirmed by quantitative analysis of the protein distribution (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantitative analysis in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Cavin3-GFP selectively increased total cellular levels of BRCA1.
source: Western blotting revealed that cavin3-GFP selective increased total cellular levels of BRCA1 (Figure 4C, quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in Figure 4C with quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cavin3 increases BRCA1 levels through a post-transcriptional effect.
source: This represents a post-transcriptional effect of cavin3 as BRCA1 mRNA levels were not significantly increased (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing no significant change in BRCA1 mRNA levels in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The proteasome inhibitor MG132 increased BRCA1 levels in control cells.
source: Interestingly, the proteasome inhibitor, MG132, increased BRCA1 levels in control cells, consistent with evidence for proteasomal degradation of BRCA1 (Choudhury et al., 2004).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis in Figure 4D and is consistent with published literature (Choudhury et al., 2004).

claim: MG132 did not increase the already-elevated levels of BRCA1 found in cavin3-GFP cells.
source: However, it did not increase the already-elevated levels of BRCA1 found in cavin3-GFP cells (Figure 4D, quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis in Figure 4D with quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cavin3 depletion caused a significant decrease in BRCA1 in A431 and MDA-MB231 cells.
source: These cell lines express cavin3, CAV1, and BRCA1 proteins and present caveolae at the plasma membrane (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E). In both cases, cavin3 depletion caused a significant decrease in BRCA1 (Figure 4E, quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, C), and this was abrogated by proteasome inhibition (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis after siRNA-mediated knockdown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Proteasome inhibition abrogated the decrease in BRCA1 caused by cavin3 depletion.
source: In both cases, cavin3 depletion caused a significant decrease in BRCA1 (Figure 4E, quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, C), and this was abrogated by proteasome inhibition (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis with MG132 treatment shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Depletion of BRCA1 significantly decreased endogenous cavin3 protein levels in A431 and MDA-MB231 cells.
source: Interestingly, depletion of BRCA1 with two independent siRNAs significantly decreased endogenous cavin3 protein levels in these cells (Figure 4F, quantitation in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, D).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis after siRNA-mediated knockdown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The total association between endogenous cavin3 and endogenous BRCA1 was significantly increased by hypo-osmotic stimulation.
source: The total association between endogenous cavin3 and endogenous BRCA1, and their association in the nucleus, was significantly increased by hypo-osmotic stimulation, as measured by PLA (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by proximity ligation assay in A431 cells shown in Figure 5A with quantitation in Figure 5E.

claim: The association between endogenous cavin3 and endogenous BRCA1 in the nucleus was significantly increased by hypo-osmotic stimulation.
source: The total association between endogenous cavin3 and endogenous BRCA1, and their association in the nucleus, was significantly increased by hypo-osmotic stimulation, as measured by PLA (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by proximity ligation assay with nuclear/cytosolic quantitation shown in Figure 5A and 5E.

claim: Mechanical disassembly of caveolae promotes the association of cavin3 with BRCA1 both in the cytosol and the nucleus.
source: These findings suggested that mechanical disassembly of caveolae could promote the association of cavin3 with BRCA1 both in the cytosol and the nucleus.
evidence: This is inferred from the PLA experiments showing increased cavin3-BRCA1 interaction after hypo-osmotic treatment.

claim: The interaction between endogenous BRCA1 and cavin3 was increased by UV exposure.
source: PLA showed that the interaction between endogenous BRCA1 and cavin3 was increased by both these stimuli (Figure 6A–D, top panel, quantitation in Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by proximity ligation assay after UV treatment shown in Figure 6B with quantitation in Figure 6E.

claim: The interaction between endogenous BRCA1 and cavin3 was increased by oxidative stress with hydrogen peroxide.
source: PLA showed that the interaction between endogenous BRCA1 and cavin3 was increased by both these stimuli (Figure 6A–D, top panel, quantitation in Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by proximity ligation assay after H2O2 treatment shown in Figure 6C with quantitation in Figure 6E.

claim: Association between BRCA1 and cavin3 was evident at 30 min and maintained at low levels for up to 4 hr after UV treatment.
source: A more extended time course further demonstrated that association between these proteins was evident at 30 min and maintained at low levels for up to 4 hr (Figure 6F, G).
evidence: This is shown by time-course PLA analysis in Figure 6F.

claim: UV treatment decreased the interaction between cavin3 and cavin1.
source: Interestingly, this coincided with a decrease in the interaction between cavin3 and cavin1, which occurs in caveolae (Figure 6A–D, bottom panel, quantitation in Figure 6G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by proximity ligation assay showing decreased cavin3-cavin1 interaction after stress treatments in Figure 6 with quantitation in Figure 6G.

claim: LDH release was consistently increased after 2 min UV exposure in MCF7 cells that overexpressed cavin3-GFP.
source: We found that LDH release, used as an index of membrane damage, was consistently increased after 2 min UV exposure in MCF7 cells that overexpressed cavin3-GFP, but not with cavin1-GFP (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays shown in Figure 7A.

claim: LDH release after UV exposure in MCF7 cells overexpressing cavin1-GFP was not increased compared to control.
source: We found that LDH release, used as an index of membrane damage, was consistently increased after 2 min UV exposure in MCF7 cells that overexpressed cavin3-GFP, but not with cavin1-GFP (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Cell damage from UV exposure in cavin3-GFP overexpressing MCF7 cells reflected apoptosis induction confirmed by annexin V staining.
source: This cell damage reflected apoptosis induction confirmed by staining for annexin V (which marks early apoptosis, Figure 7B) and the DNA dye 7-amino-actinomycin 7 (7-AAD, late apoptosis, Figure 7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis of annexin V staining shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Cell damage from UV exposure in cavin3-GFP overexpressing MCF7 cells reflected apoptosis induction confirmed by 7-AAD staining.
source: This cell damage reflected apoptosis induction confirmed by staining for annexin V (which marks early apoptosis, Figure 7B) and the DNA dye 7-amino-actinomycin 7 (7-AAD, late apoptosis, Figure 7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis of 7-AAD staining shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Cavin3 sensitizes MCF7 cells to UV-induced apoptosis.
source: Thus, cavin3 could sensitize MCF7 cells to UV-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is concluded from the LDH release, annexin V, and 7-AAD staining experiments shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: Overexpression of cavin3-GFP significantly increased LDH release from UV-treated A431 and MDA-MB231 cells.
source: Indeed, overexpression of cavin3-GFP significantly increased LDH release from UV-treated A431 and MDA-MB231 cells (Figure 7D, F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays shown in Figure 7D and 7F.

claim: Depletion of endogenous cavin3 reduced LDH release from A431 and MDA-MB231 cells after UV stimulation.
source: Furthermore, depletion of endogenous cavin3 reduced LDH release from these cells after UV stimulation (Figure 7E, G, controls in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays after siRNA-mediated knockdown shown in Figure 7E and 7G.

claim: BRCA1 sensitized A431 and MDA-MB231 cells to apoptosis.
source: BRCA1 also sensitized A431 and MDA-MB231 cells to apoptosis, as evident when exogenous BRCA1 was overexpressed or the endogenous protein was depleted (Figure 7E, G, controls in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays with BRCA1 overexpression and knockdown shown in Figure 7E and 7G.

claim: Overexpression of BRCA1 in cavin3-depleted A431 or MDA-MB231 cells restored UV-induced apoptosis to control levels.
source: Overexpression of BRCA1 in cavin3-depleted A431 or MDA-MB231 cells or overexpression of cavin3 in BRCA1-depleted cells restored UV-induced apoptosis to control levels.
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays with rescue experiments shown in Figure 7E and 7G.

claim: Overexpression of cavin3 in BRCA1-depleted A431 or MDA-MB231 cells restored UV-induced apoptosis to control levels.
source: Overexpression of BRCA1 in cavin3-depleted A431 or MDA-MB231 cells or overexpression of cavin3 in BRCA1-depleted cells restored UV-induced apoptosis to control levels.
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH release assays with rescue experiments shown in Figure 7E and 7G.

claim: BRCA1 and cavin3 have a similar sensitizing effect on UV-induced apoptosis.
source: This indicated that these two proteins have a similar sensitizing effect on UV-induced apoptosis (Figure 7E, G).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that either protein can restore UV sensitivity.

claim: Cavin3 KO HeLa cells exhibited enhanced resistance to hypo-osmotic stress, UV, and oxidative stress.
source: Cavin3 KO cells exhibited enhanced resistance to all stressors, and apart from oxidative stress, this was time-dependent (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PrestoBlue cell viability assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: BRCA1 and cavin3 participate together in the cellular stress response.
source: Overall, these findings suggest that BRCA1 and cavin3 participate together in the cellular stress response.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined apoptosis and stress resistance experiments.

claim: UV treatment of WT HeLa cells upregulated the expression of cavin3, BRCA1, RAD51, and the A-complex proteins MDC1, Rap80, RNF168, and Merit40.
source: As shown in Figure 8A–C, UV treatment of WT cells upregulated the expression of cavin3, BRCA1, the DNA damage marker, RAD51, and the A-complex proteins MDC1, Rap80, RNF168, and Merit40.
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis after UV treatment shown in Figure 8A and 8C.

claim: The upregulation of BRCA1, RAD51, and the BRCA1 A-complex proteins was dramatically reduced in cavin3 KO cells after UV treatment.
source: Strikingly, the upregulation of BRCA1, RAD51, and the BRCA1 A-complex proteins was dramatically reduced in cavin3 KO cells (Figure 8A, C, quantitation in Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis comparing WT and cavin3 KO cells after UV treatment shown in Figure 8A and 8C.

claim: Cavin3 influences the ability of BRCA1 to repair damaged DNA.
source: This suggested that cavin3 can influence the ability of BRCA1 to repair damaged DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced upregulation of DNA repair proteins in cavin3 KO cells after UV treatment.

claim: BRCA1 foci increased within 30 min of UV irradiation in WT HeLa cells.
source: Indeed, we found that BRCA1 foci increased within 30 min of UV irradiation (Figure 8D, E); however, this was significantly reduced in cavin3 KO cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantitation shown in Figure 8D and 8E.

claim: BRCA1 foci formation after UV irradiation was significantly reduced in cavin3 KO cells.
source: Indeed, we found that BRCA1 foci increased within 30 min of UV irradiation (Figure 8D, E); however, this was significantly reduced in cavin3 KO cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantitation shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The recruitment of RAP80 after UV irradiation was reduced in cavin3 KO cells.
source: Similarly, the recruitment of RAP80 and γH2AX was reduced in cavin3 KO cells, suggesting that DNA repair might be fundamentally compromised in these cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantitation shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The recruitment of γH2AX after UV irradiation was reduced in cavin3 KO cells.
source: Similarly, the recruitment of RAP80 and γH2AX was reduced in cavin3 KO cells, suggesting that DNA repair might be fundamentally compromised in these cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantitation shown in Figure 8E.

claim: DNA repair is fundamentally compromised in cavin3 KO cells.
source: Similarly, the recruitment of RAP80 and γH2AX was reduced in cavin3 KO cells, suggesting that DNA repair might be fundamentally compromised in these cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced recruitment of DNA repair proteins to damage sites.

claim: Loss of functional BRCA1 protein leads to defects in DSB repair by homologous recombination and renders cells hypersensitive to PARP inhibitors.
source: Previous studies have shown that loss of functional BRCA1 protein leads to defects in DSB repair by homologous recombination and renders cells hypersensitive to PARP inhibitors through the mechanism of synthetic lethality (Ashworth, 2008; Bryant et al., 2005; Farmer et al., 2005; Helleday et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on multiple published studies (Ashworth, 2008; Bryant et al., 2005; Farmer et al., 2005; Helleday et al., 2005).

claim: Cavin3-deficient HeLa cells were more sensitive to the PARP inhibitor AZD2461 than control WT HeLa cells.
source: Clonogenic survival assays and cell viability studies revealed that cavin3-deficient HeLa cells (red dots) were more sensitive to the PARP inhibitor AZD2461 at nM concentrations than control WT HeLa cells (black dots, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by clonogenic survival assays and cell viability studies shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cavin3 and PARP1 double KO cells failed to produce colonies in clonogenic survival assays with reduced cell viability.
source: Cavin3 and PARP1 KO cells failed to produce colonies in clonogenic survival assays with reduced cell viability (pink dots, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by clonogenic survival assays and cell viability studies shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cavin3-deficient HeLa cells are sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that cavin3 and BRCA1 are involved in homologous recombination repair.
source: These findings suggest that cavin3-deficient HeLa cells are sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that cavin3 and BRCA1 are involved in homologous recombination repair.
evidence: This is inferred from the PARP inhibitor sensitivity experiments.

claim: PARP1 is a potential synthetic lethal partner for cavin3.
source: Furthermore, these findings suggest that PARP1 is a potential synthetic lethal partner for cavin3.
evidence: This is inferred from the synthetic lethality observed in cavin3 and PARP1 double KO cells.

claim: PARP-treated cavin3 KO cells showed increased DNA damage following a 6-day treatment as measured by comet assay.
source: We evaluated DNA strand breaks in control and PARP-treated WT HeLa and cavin3 KO cells using a comet assay, which revealed increased DNA damage only in PARP-treated cavin3 KO cells following a 6-day treatment (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comet assay analysis shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Loss of 53BP1 partially restores homologous recombination repair in BRCA1-deficient cells.
source: Recent reports have linked 53BP1 loss to PARP inhibitor resistance, presumably, as loss of 53BP1 partially restores homologous recombination repair in BRCA1-deficient cells (Bouwman et al., 2010; Bunting et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2009; Turner et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated based on multiple published studies (Bouwman et al., 2010; Bunting et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2009; Turner et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2017).

claim: Loss of 53BP1 in cavin3 HeLa KO cells reverted the PARP sensitivity of these cells to WT cell levels.
source: Loss of 53BP1 in cavin3 HeLa KO cells could revert the PARP sensitivity of these cells to WT cell levels as demonstrated in clonogenic survival and cell viability assays (orange dots, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by clonogenic survival and cell viability assays shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Homologous recombination DNA repair is partially restored in BRCA1-deficient cells following 53BP1 loss.
source: These findings agree with several studies demonstrating that homologous recombination DNA repair is partially restored in BRCA1-deficient cells following 53BP1 loss (Bouwman et al., 2010; Bunting et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2009; Turner et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated based on multiple published studies (Bouwman et al., 2010; Bunting et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2009; Turner et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2017).

claim: Depletion of CHD3 specifically in cavin3 KO cells induced profound cellular sensitivity to PARP inhibition.
source: Depletion of CHD3 and FANCD2 specifically in cavin3 KO cells induced profound cellular sensitivity to PARP inhibition in clonogenic survival and cell viability assays (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by clonogenic survival and cell viability assays shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Depletion of FANCD2 specifically in cavin3 KO cells induced profound cellular sensitivity to PARP inhibition.
source: Depletion of CHD3 and FANCD2 specifically in cavin3 KO cells induced profound cellular sensitivity to PARP inhibition in clonogenic survival and cell viability assays (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by clonogenic survival and cell viability assays shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cavin3 KO cells represent a novel cellular system to dissect interactions in the DNA damage response.
source: These findings suggest that cavin3 KO cells represent a novel cellular system to begin to dissect the interactions that occur in the DNA damage response, compensated that may occur by other components in a similar or different pathway for cell survival, and how this information can be used to identify new drug agents and treatment strategies in cancer.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings with cavin3 KO cells.

claim: Caveolae can act as general sensors and transducers of cellular stress by releasing cavins.
source: Our studies raise the intriguing possibility that by releasing cavins, which can be triggered by mechanical and non-mechanical stimuli such as UV and oxidative stress (McMahon et al., 2019, and this study), caveolae can act as general sensors and transducers of cellular stress.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings showing stress-induced cavin release and interaction with BRCA1.

claim: The possibility of an interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3 was first suggested some 20 years ago.
source: The possibility of an interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3 was first suggested some 20 years ago, yet, no experimental evidence to support this interaction has been published to date (Xu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated based on a previous publication (Xu et al., 2001).

claim: No experimental evidence to support the interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3 has been published prior to this study.
source: The possibility of an interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3 was first suggested some 20 years ago, yet, no experimental evidence to support this interaction has been published to date (Xu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated based on the lack of published experimental evidence prior to this study.

claim: This study provides the first clear evidence that cavin3 directly interacts with BRCA1.
source: Our results provide the first clear evidence that cavin3 directly interacts with BRCA1 and that this occurs when cavin3 is released from caveolae in response to cellular stressors.
evidence: This is concluded from the multiple experimental approaches used in this study.

claim: The interaction between cavin3 and BRCA1 occurs when cavin3 is released from caveolae in response to cellular stressors.
source: Our results provide the first clear evidence that cavin3 directly interacts with BRCA1 and that this occurs when cavin3 is released from caveolae in response to cellular stressors.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the PLA experiments showing increased interaction after stress treatments.

claim: Coimmunoprecipitation failed to reproducibly detect the interaction between BRCA1 and cavin3.
source: We were not able to reproducibly coimmunoprecipitate BRCA1 and cavin3. However, this technique can fail to detect weak or transient interactions (Berggård et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a negative result with explanation based on published literature (Berggård et al., 2007).

claim: Coimmunoprecipitation can fail to detect weak or transient interactions.
source: We were not able to reproducibly coimmunoprecipitate BRCA1 and cavin3. However, this technique can fail to detect weak or transient interactions (Berggård et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated based on published literature (Berggård et al., 2007).

claim: Cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via direct interaction with the RING domain of BRCA1.
source: We propose that cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via multiple mechanisms: direct interaction with the RING domain of BRCA1 (Figure 2J), increased localization of BRCA1 to the cytosol (Figure 4A, B), regulation of BRCA1 protein levels (Figure 4C, F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), modulation of proteasome-mediated protein degradation (Figure 4G), by facilitating the localization of components of the BRCA1-A-complex in response to UV-induced DNA damage (Figure 8E) and in DNA repair, as cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that these cells are deficient in homologous recombination DNA repair (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is proposed based on the cell-free expression experiments showing interaction with the N-terminal region containing the RING domain.

claim: Cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via increased localization of BRCA1 to the cytosol.
source: We propose that cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via multiple mechanisms: direct interaction with the RING domain of BRCA1 (Figure 2J), increased localization of BRCA1 to the cytosol (Figure 4A, B), regulation of BRCA1 protein levels (Figure 4C, F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), modulation of proteasome-mediated protein degradation (Figure 4G), by facilitating the localization of components of the BRCA1-A-complex in response to UV-induced DNA damage (Figure 8E) and in DNA repair, as cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that these cells are deficient in homologous recombination DNA repair (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is proposed based on the immunofluorescence data showing increased cytosolic BRCA1 in cavin3-expressing cells.

claim: Cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via regulation of BRCA1 protein levels.
source: We propose that cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via multiple mechanisms: direct interaction with the RING domain of BRCA1 (Figure 2J), increased localization of BRCA1 to the cytosol (Figure 4A, B), regulation of BRCA1 protein levels (Figure 4C, F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), modulation of proteasome-mediated protein degradation (Figure 4G), by facilitating the localization of components of the BRCA1-A-complex in response to UV-induced DNA damage (Figure 8E) and in DNA repair, as cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that these cells are deficient in homologous recombination DNA repair (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is proposed based on the western blot data showing cavin3-dependent changes in BRCA1 protein levels.

claim: Cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via modulation of proteasome-mediated protein degradation.
source: We propose that cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via multiple mechanisms: direct interaction with the RING domain of BRCA1 (Figure 2J), increased localization of BRCA1 to the cytosol (Figure 4A, B), regulation of BRCA1 protein levels (Figure 4C, F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), modulation of proteasome-mediated protein degradation (Figure 4G), by facilitating the localization of components of the BRCA1-A-complex in response to UV-induced DNA damage (Figure 8E) and in DNA repair, as cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that these cells are deficient in homologous recombination DNA repair (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is proposed based on the MG132 experiments showing proteasome-dependent regulation.

claim: Cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function by facilitating the localization of components of the BRCA1-A-complex in response to UV-induced DNA damage.
source: We propose that cavin3 can modulate BRCA1 function via multiple mechanisms: direct interaction with the RING domain of BRCA1 (Figure 2J), increased localization of BRCA1 to the cytosol (Figure 4A, B), regulation of BRCA1 protein levels (Figure 4C, F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), modulation of proteasome-mediated protein degradation (Figure 4G), by facilitating the localization of components of the BRCA1-A-complex in response to UV-induced DNA damage (Figure 8E) and in DNA repair, as cavin3-deficient cells were sensitive to PARP inhibition, suggesting that these cells are deficient in homologous recombination DNA repair (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is proposed based on the foci formation experiments showing reduced recruitment of BRCA1 A-complex components in cavin3 KO cells.

claim: The ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation pathway plays a role in the coordinated protein stability of BRCA1 and cavin3.
source: We show that the ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation pathway plays a role in the coordinated protein stability of BRCA1 and cavin3 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the MG132 proteasome inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The RING domain region of BRCA1 is the degron sequence necessary for polyubiquitination and proteasome-mediated protein degradation.
source: Previous studies have identified the RING domain region of BRCA1 as the degron sequence necessary for polyubiquitination and proteasome-mediated protein degradation, which coincides with the interaction domain of BRCA1 identified here for cavin3 (Lu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated based on published literature (Lu et al., 2007).

claim: The RING domain region of BRCA1 coincides with the interaction domain of BRCA1 identified for cavin3.
